I've been working this land for 50 years and I know what grows here. Quzhou sits on the North China Plain — dry winters, hot summers, and my well keeps me from depending on rain. At 70, my son is off working in the city, so it's mostly just me and my wife now. I can't push myself like I used to, so I keep things practical and familiar.

**Wheat (October planting):**
I'll put all 30 mu into wheat after the maize comes off. I always use the improved variety — Jimai 22 is what I've trusted for years. I'll do rotary tillage to turn under the maize stubble, same as always. I'll apply base fertilizer before sowing — diammonium phosphate and urea — and topdress at jointing. I need at least 3 irrigations: one before winter sets in, one at jointing, one at heading. I'll spray herbicide in December when the weeds come up, and a fungicide around heading time to hold off the powdery mildew. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize (June planting, right after wheat harvest):**
No time to waste between crops — I'll go straight to planting after wheat harvest without tilling. My knees don't appreciate the extra passes anyway, and the soil is fine. I'll use Xianyu 335, the hybrid — everyone in the village uses it and it yields well. Summer gets enough rain that I only need to irrigate twice, maybe three times if July turns dry. One herbicide pass early, one insecticide spray when the corn borer pressure picks up around August.
